Hi Camila,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Fintegral liked the latency profile. Security has a short list of technical questions before we move to procurement:

1) For live inference of customer requests, which cloud regions can execute our traffic? We need a clear list of regions (preferably AZ-level) where processing may occur for the EU tenant.
2) Which subprocessors touch the inference path (routing, logging, backups)? We need contact names and contractual attachments where possible.
3) Can you describe the encryption/key model? Do you offer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for hosted deployments or only in Private?
4) Deletion: if a data subject or admin requests erasure, what is the timeline from acceptance to actual removal from all storage (primary, caches, backups)? Any exceptions (legal hold)?

We appreciate short, actionable answers — SOC2 evidence and a subprocessor roster would be ideal. Can you loop in whoever owns evidence packs?

Best,

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I will pull the formal evidence packet. Short summary:

- Regions: For EU tenants we primarily run inference in eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) in Hosted. We also maintain warm failover capability in us-east-1 for cross-region resilience; however, routing policy can be limited to EU-only for customers requiring residency.
- Subprocessors: The inference path includes (1) cloud compute provider (AWS), (2) our CDN partner for streaming responses, and (3) a managed logging provider used for aggregated telemetry. We'll attach the roster with legal contacts.
- Keys/encryption: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+. At-rest data (checkpoints, logs, caches) is AES-256. We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in Dedicated and Private deployments today; for Hosted customers we offer bring-your-own-key via a HSM-backed option (KMS integration) on our enterprise tier — I will confirm the onboarding steps.
- Deletion: Typical flow is: request acknowledged within 24 hours; primary storage purge within 72 hours after verification; cache/prefix eviction within 24 hours; backups retained up to a 30-day recovery window and purged in the next backup rotation unless a legal hold is active. Legal hold/e-discovery can extend retention — those are escalated to our compliance team.

I'm looping in Marissa (security evidence) and Vivek (infrastructure) to drop the SOC2 cert, subprocessor PDF, and a KMS flow diagram.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Camila — sending what I was able to compile (attached). Quick technical notes for the one-pager:

- Processing regions (EU tenant): eu-west-1 (Ireland) primary, eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) for redundancy. Warm failover in us-east-1 only if customer enables cross-region fallback; we treat US as an exception and document it in the DPA.
- Cross-border safeguards: We rely on standard contractual clauses (SCCs) with subprocessors and AWS’s adequacy/contractual measures. For enterprise customers requiring contractual language, we can add EU SCCs in our DPA or offer Dedicated/Private deployments to avoid transfers.
- Subprocessor roster (attached): AWS (compute/storage), FastStream CDN (edge streaming), Loglynx (aggregated metrics). Contacts and legal addresses are in the PDF.
- KMS model: Hosted enterprise tier — offer HSM-backed BYOK with key wrapping; Dedicated/Private — full CMK control and optional on-prem HSM integration. Diagram attached (kms_keyflow_diagram.svg).
- Deletion playbook: acceptance ack within 24h; primary datastore purge within 72h; KV/prefix cache eviction within 24h; backups pruned on a 30-day rolling window. If legal hold is invoked, we mark the record and exclude from deletion until release; we keep an audit trail for all erase requests.

Attachments in this thread: subprocessor_inventory_fintegral_20260818.pdf, soc2_type2_certificate_2025.pdf, kms_keyflow_diagram.svg, deletion_playbook.md

—Marissa
